researched_writeups.title: Pitch: Kohl's Corporation (NYSE:KSS)
researched_writeups.summary: Countervail Capital frames Kohl's equity as a 3-year call option on the net liquidation value of its 400 owned properties and 245 ground-leased stores . Scraper analysis of county-level property assessor databases reveals that despite broadline retail contractions and top-line declines, Kohl's $9.7 billion property asset base net of $7.0 billion in total debt creates a highly convex, option-like return profile in positive liquidation scenarios. The thesis identifies real estate monetization through sale-leasebacks or asset sales as the primary catalyst to unlock latent equity value.

researched_writeups.title: There is One Last Puff in Kohl's (KSS) Deep Value Play
researched_writeups.summary: Hugo Navarro presents a deep-value 'cigar-butt' thesis, arguing that extreme market pessimism and a ~50% short interest reflect misplaced fears of imminent bankruptcy. The author highlights Kohl's robust liquidity and historical track record of generating over $1 billion in annual free cash flow as downside protection. Valuing Kohl's unencumbered real estate assets minus debt yields a conservative intrinsic value between $22 and $70 per share, with operational catalysts anchored by CEO leadership and Sephora shop-in-shop growth.

researched_writeups.title: Getting Greedy While Investors Remain Fearful: Kohl's Corporation (KSS)
researched_writeups.summary: The post analyzes Kohl's trading at $12.85 per share against an estimated Net Asset Value (NAV) of $33.99 per share, representing over 160% upside. Backed by 409 owned stores and 13 distribution centers carried well below fair market value, the write-up refutes near-term default fears on upcoming bond maturities. The author demonstrates how closing 27 underperforming stores and liquidating real estate assets provides necessary liquidity to service debt and re-rate shares toward tangible asset value.

researched_writeups.title: Is There Hidden Value at Heavily Shorted Kohl's $KSS
researched_writeups.summary: This Reddit deep-dive evaluates Kohl's as an asset-backed turnaround opportunity where owned real estate and fulfillment infrastructure, estimated at ~$8 billion, dwarf the company's depressed market cap. The analysis details unit economics strengthened by the Sephora store-within-a-store rollout, debt paydowns, and ongoing free cash flow generation ($100M+ in 2024, $500M+ in 2023). With 42% short interest and institutional ownership exceeding 100% of the float, strategic real estate sales or buyback announcements serve as key re-rating catalysts.
